claims.quote: Billions of image-text pairs, ranging from social media posts to news articles and e-commerce listings, are now freely available at web scale, providing a rich and diverse source of supervision for training multimodal models without the need for costly manual annotation [1].
The fundamental motivation behind VLP is to overcome these limitations by learning universal, transferable multimodal representations from large-scale, weakly supervised data [4].

The introduction of Vision Transformers (ViTs) represented a major architectural shift, applying the transformer architecture—originally developed for NLP—directly to image patches, achieving competitive or superior performance compared to CNNs on standard benchmarks [21].
Multi-task training further reinforced this view by demonstrating that jointly learning across multiple VL tasks with a single model could improve performance compared to task-specific baselines [3].

The choice of visual encoder critically impacts the quality and efficiency of cross-modal alignment. Early VLP models relied on pretrained object detectors such as Faster R-CNN to extract region-based visual features, which provide semantically rich representations but introduce computational bottlenecks, restrict the concept vocabulary to the detector's training categories, and decouple visual and cross-modal learning [34].

More recent architectures such as BEiT-3 [13] generalized masked image modeling—itself inspired by BERT's masked language modeling—to image tokens represented as visual "words," treating images as a foreign language to be processed by the same transformer backbone used for text.

BEiT-3 pretrains by performing masked data modeling across monomodal and multimodal data simultaneously, treating image patches, text tokens, and image-text pairs uniformly within the same transformer framework.

The [77] model exemplifies this integration philosophy by employing a single transformer network that is shared across image encoding, text encoding, and multimodal fusion tasks. UFO jointly optimizes image-text contrastive loss, image-text matching loss, and masked language modeling loss within a unified architecture by leveraging both bidirectional and seq2seq attention masks.

Models such as SimVLM [4] have reported substantial gains on VQA v2, achieving improvements of +3.74% vqa-score over prior pretraining methods, demonstrating how large-scale weak supervision with prefix language modeling objectives can dramatically improve VQA performance.
The VLUE benchmark [57] explicitly incorporates out-of-distribution test sets and efficiency-performance trade-off measures, providing a more honest assessment of VLP model generalization—

The MMVP benchmark has revealed CLIP-blind pairs—visually distinct images that contrastive models erroneously perceive as semantically similar—exposing systematic visual shortcomings that aggregate retrieval metrics fail to detect.

Future research must develop principled methods for auditing and mitigating social biases absorbed from web-scale training corpora, building on emerging debiasing and counterfactual evaluation frameworks.
